27	 * region derived from the postcode (see {@link Regions#regionOfPostcode(String)}) and HASH8 is the
28	 * first 8 upper-case hex characters of SHA-256 over the normalized telephone concatenated with the
29	 * last name (e.g. {@code 'NSW-1A2B3C4D'}).
30	 */
31	@Component
32	public class CustomerCodeGenerator {
33	
34	    private static final int HASH_LENGTH = 8;
35	
36	    /**
37	     * @param postcode  the owner's postcode, used to derive the REGION prefix
38	     * @param telephone the owner's normalized telephone, hashed with the last name
39	     * @param lastName  the owner's last name, hashed with the telephone
40	     * @return the formatted customer code
41	     */
42	    public String generate(String postcode, String telephone, String lastName) {
43	        String region = Regions.regionOfPostcode(postcode);
44	        String hash8 = Sha256.hex(telephone + lastName).substring(0, HASH_LENGTH).toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT);

23	/**
24	 * Canonical identity of a household. Two owners belong to the same household when they share a last
25	 * name and postcode, the last name compared case-insensitively and with collapsed whitespace. This
26	 * class is the single place that decides that equivalence so duplicate detection, household-size
27	 * counting and household-id assignment stay in agreement.
28	 */
29	@Component
30	public class HouseholdKey {
31	
32	    /**
33	     * @param lastName the owner's last name
34	     * @param postcode the owner's postcode
35	     * @return a canonical key {@code normalizedLastName + '|' + postcode} such that owners in the
36	     * same household produce equal keys
37	     */
38	    public String of(String lastName, String postcode) {
39	        return normalize(lastName) + "|" + (postcode == null ? "" : postcode);
40	    }
41	
42	    /** Lower-case and collapse runs of whitespace to a single space so trivial formatting
43	     *  differences do not defeat the household comparison. */
44	    private static String normalize(String value) {
45	        if (value == null) {
46	            return "";
47	        }
48	        return value.trim().replaceAll("\\s+", " ").toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT);
49	    }
50	}

Here is the complete, ordered list of every validation and side-effect applied when creating an owner via `POST /api/owners`. The endpoint is `OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner(OwnerFieldsDto)` (implementing the generated `OwnersApi`). The request body binds to the generated **`OwnerFieldsDto`**, not the `Owner` entity.

## Phase 0 — Framework Bean Validation (`@Valid @RequestBody`)

Runs before the method body. On failure → **400** (`MethodArgumentNotValidException`).

- `firstName` — `@NotNull`, `@Size(1..30)`, `@Pattern(^[\p{L}]+([ '-][\p{L}]+){0,2}$)`
- `lastName` — `@NotNull`, `@Size(1..30)`, `@Pattern(^[\p{L}]+([ '-][\p{L}]+){0,2}\.?$)`
- `address` — `@NotNull`, `@Size(1..255)`
- `city` — `@NotNull`, `@Size(1..80)`
- `telephone` — `@NotNull`, `@Size(1..20)`
- `email` — `@Size(max 255)` (optional)
- `postcode` — **no** bean constraint (validated imperatively later)
- `registrationDate` / `birthDate` — `@Valid` only; `sharesHousehold` — none (defaults `false`)

## Phase 1 — Imperative validators & normalizers (controller body, in this exact order)

1. **`addressNormalizer.normalize(address)`** — *side-effect*: trims/collapses whitespace, upper-cases, expands ST→STREET / RD→ROAD / AVE→AVENUE; mutates the DTO's address. (Runs before the required-field check, so that check sees the normalized value.)
2. **`ownerRequestValidator.validate`** — required-fields check on firstName/lastName/address/city/telephone (`hasText`) → `RequiredFieldsMissingException` **400**.
3. **`postcodeValidator.validate`** — if postcode present: must be 4 digits and within the region range for the city → `InvalidPostcodeException` **400**.
4. **`cityOwnerLimitValidator.validate`** — DB count; `>= 50` owners in that city → `CityOwnerLimitExceededException` **409**.
5. **`registrationDateValidator.validate`** — supplied date after today → `FutureRegistrationDateException` **400**.
6. **`dailyOwnerLimitValidator.validate`** — rolls date to a business day; `>= 100` owners registered that day → `DailyOwnerLimitExceededException` **429**.
7. **`telephoneNormalizer.normalize(telephone)`** — *side-effect*: normalizes to E.164 (default country `+61`, strips formatting, drops one leading `0`); requires 8–15 digits / valid national length; else `InvalidTelephoneException` **400**. Mutates the DTO telephone.
8. **`emailNormalizer.normalize(email)`** — *side-effect*: null/blank → `null`; else must match email regex (`InvalidEmailException` **400**), returns trimmed + lower-cased. Mutates the DTO email.
9. **`disposableEmailDomainValidator.validate(email)`** — blocks mailinator.com / tempmail.com / guerrillamail.com → `DisposableEmailDomainException` **400**.

## Phase 2 — Mapping & derived-field side-effects (all before save)

10. **`ownerMapper.toOwner(dto)`** — builds the `Owner` entity (ignores `id` and `pets`).
11. **`householdIdGenerator.generate(lastName, postcode)`** → sets `householdId` (first 12 hex of SHA-256 of the household key).
12. **Duplicate handling**, branching on `sharesHousehold`:
    - If `true`: sets `possibleDuplicate = false`, `possibleDuplicateOf = null` (no duplicate check).
    - If `false`: **`duplicateOwnerValidator.validate`** — loads all owners, hard-fails on same household key (lastName+postcode) → `DuplicateOwnerException` **409**; then **`possibleDuplicateDetector.findPossibleDuplicate`** (soft, never throws) → sets `possibleDuplicate` flag + `possibleDuplicateOf` id.
13. **`customerCodeGenerator.generate(postcode, telephone, lastName)`** → sets `customerCode` (`<REGION>-<HASH8>`).
14. **`clinicService.countNamesakes(firstName, lastName)`** → sets `namesakeCount`.
15. **`householdSizeCalculator.size(owner)`** → sets `householdSize` (counts same-household owners + 1).

## Phase 3 — Persistence

16. **`clinicService.saveOwner(owner)`** → `ownerRepository.save` → JPA `persist`, which triggers the entity's **`@PrePersist resolveRegistrationDate()`**: if `registrationDate` is null, defaults it to `LocalDate.now()`, then adjusts it forward to a business day (`BusinessDay.onOrAfter`). Hibernate also validates the entity's own `@NotEmpty`/`@Pattern` constraints (including telephone `^\+[0-9]{8,15}$`) on flush.

## Phase 4 — Post-save side-effects & response

17. **`ownerAuditLogger.created(owner)`** — SLF4J log to the `"AUDIT"` logger (id, customerCode, registrationDate, membershipLevel).
18. **Response DTO** — `ownerMapper.toOwnerDto`, plus **`bulkSignupWarningEvaluator.isBulkSignupInEffect()`** set on the DTO (true when > 80 owners registered today).
19. Sets `Location: /api/owners/{id}` header, returns **201 CREATED**.

---

Two ordering nuances worth flagging:

- **Normalizers mutate the request DTO in place** before downstream validators run — e.g. address normalization happens before the required-field check, and telephone/email normalization happens before their respective format/domain validators.
- **`registrationDate` is finalized only at `@PrePersist` (step 16)**, *after* the registration-date and daily-limit validators (steps 5–6) and after all derived fields are computed. So any field derived from the registration date before save can diverge from the value actually persisted when the client omits the date or supplies a weekend/holiday date.

I read the code only; nothing was changed.
